history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx), initiated by Harvard University, was designed to explore the behavior of small aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Led by principal investigator Frank Keutsch and his team, including David Keith, this research was introduced at the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017. The objective was to improve computer models assessing the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering, particularly solar radiation management, without implementing actual geoengineering strategies or attempting to cool the planet. The experiment proposed to release a small quantity of calcium carbonate—between 100 grams and 2 kilograms—into a controlled volume, using a scientific balloon gondola at an altitude of approximately 20 km to study aerosol microphysics and light scattering. A planned hardware test in Sweden was postponed in 2021 pending further societal engagement, and no particles were released. As of March 2024, Harvard announced that Keutsch would no longer continue with SCoPEx, and the platform will be redirected for different stratospheric research initiatives. #geoengineering
